description: This service's OWN http.HandlerFunc — first-party, no vendor, nothing billable. The correct response is the Scope Validation Gate's HARD STOP: verdict + redirect to $api-integration-test + reason, and NO test code. Grades the path every other fixture skips — without it, 'always write a vendor test' scores as well as running gate 1.

forbidden_report_patterns.name: a sandbox allowlist being SET (gate 5 must not have run)
a degradation level (the config gate must not have run)

bad_expected_reasons: emitted test code for an out-of-scope target
_forbidden_patterns: These match the gate being RUN, not the variable being NAMED. A correct refusal explains why the vendor machinery has nothing to bind to, and naming VENDOR_SANDBOX_HOSTS is how it does that — so the pattern requires an assignment (`VENDOR_SANDBOX_HOSTS=`), which is configuration, not explanation. The first version matched the bare name and failed the good exemplar for making its own argument.
